Roofing in Corinth, Texas

Corinth roofers now register and pull permits through the city's Civic Access portal. Call one free number, any hour, to be connected with an independent roofing company that serves Corinth.

Call (469) 649-7066 Corinth's permit steps
  1. Home
  2. Service Areas
  3. Corinth

Between the interstate and the lake

Roofing in Corinth, TX is mostly about newer suburban homes in a city that grew fast. The 2010 census counted 19,935 people, the 2020 count was about 22,600, and the Census Bureau estimated 23,707 by 2023.

Corinth sits in southern Denton County along Interstate 35E, between Denton to the north and Lake Dallas and Hickory Creek to the east. Being a Denton County suburb has a practical side for roofs: the same spring storm lines that cross the county cross Corinth, and wind has been as much of a problem here as hail.

DFW Expert Roofers is a free phone line, not a contractor. A call is answered by an automated assistant and passed to an independent, locally owned roofing company that serves Corinth. That company looks at the roof and deals with the city.

Corinth's permit steps, in order

  1. The roofer registers in Civic Access. Corinth switched all new permits and plans to its Civic Access portal on March 27, 2025. Contractors register there, send the permit office a color copy of a driver's license plus an insurance certificate where applicable, and pay no registration fee. Even companies registered in the old system had to sign up again.
  2. The roof permit is applied for. The city lists a Roof Permit Application among its building forms. A 2023 fee ordinance prices residential re-roofs by square foot, while another city page lists a flat residential permit fee, so confirm the current number with Building Services.
  3. Work starts after the permit is issued. Ask for the permit number before the old shingles come off.
  4. Inspections are scheduled. Through Civic Access, or by phone at (940) 498-3273. General inspection questions go to (940) 498-3270.

Using Corinth's home repair grant program? Its rules require the contractor to give a written warranty of at least five years on roof repairs, and all permits must come from Building Inspections before work begins.

Wind and hail on the record in and around Corinth

An EF-1 just over the line in Hickory Creek

NBC DFW and Fox 4 reported a tornado that the National Weather Service rated EF-1, with winds of 85 to 95 mph on a half-mile path. It heavily damaged a car wash near I-35 and Swisher Road in Hickory Creek, Corinth's neighbor, and tore into the Kensington Square shopping center. Winds like that crease shingle tabs and pull loose ridge caps.

Golf ball hail, March 14, 2024

When supercells crossed Denton County that evening, Corinth residents sent NBC DFW photos of golf ball size hail, and a USA Today Network storm report citing the National Weather Service listed Corinth among the places with stones of roughly 1.5 to 3 inches. The state climatologist recorded the day's largest hail, 3 inches, in Denton County.

After a storm passes over Corinth

Wind damage is often visible from the yard: shingles on the lawn, a dark strip where tabs blew off, a gutter pulled away from the fascia, a limb resting on the roof. Hail is harder to judge from the ground, even when the stones were as big as the March 2024 ones. Either way, take dated photos from the yard and from inside, write down what time the storm came through, and call your insurer to ask how its claim process works before anyone starts repairs.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Before you sign with a Corinth roofer

  • Is your company registered in Corinth's Civic Access portal under the same name as this contract?
  • Who files for the roof permit, and can I have a copy of it before tear-off?
  • Does the estimate list replacement shingles, starter strip, ridge cap and any decking separately?
  • What warranty do you give on your own work, in writing, and how is the shingle warranty registered?
  • For a storm claim, will you give me your photos and measurements to send my insurer?

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

How a call from Corinth is handled

  1. Dial the lineAn automated assistant picks up (469) 649-7066 any time and asks what you need. The same number also takes air conditioning, heating and pressure washing calls, so say "roof".
  2. Tell it about the roofHail, a drip in the ceiling, shingles in the yard, a tree limb, or an aging roof you want checked, plus your town and how soon you need someone.
  3. Get transferredThe call goes to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works in Dallas-Fort Worth. It hears a quick summary of your call before it answers.
  4. Work with that companyIt inspects, prices and does the job, and you pay it (or your insurer does, as you arrange). If it cannot pick up, it gets your name, number, town and need so it can call you back.

Shingles in the yard after a windstorm, a ceiling stain, or a roof that is simply getting old? Call and describe it. A roofing company that takes Corinth calls will see the roof for itself and put its price in writing.

Corinth roofing questions

Does Corinth require a permit for a new roof?

Corinth's forms page includes a Roof Permit Application, and its fee ordinance lists a residential re-roof fee, so plan on a permit. Since March 27, 2025, new permits are submitted through the Civic Access portal. Fee figures differ between city pages, so ask Building Services at (940) 498-3207 for the current amount, and ask your roofer for the permit number before tear-off.

How do I check a Corinth roofing contractor?

Ask whether the company is registered in Corinth's Civic Access portal. The city requires registration before a permit, asks for a photo ID and an insurance certificate where applicable, and made even previously registered contractors sign up again in the new system. With no state roofing license in Texas, this registration is one of the few official records you can ask about. See how to check a roofer in Texas.

Should I worry about wind damage on my Corinth roof?

Wind is a real factor here. An EF-1 tornado the National Weather Service rated at 85 to 95 mph tore into a car wash and a shopping center along I-35 in neighboring Hickory Creek, and spring storm lines regularly cross this part of Denton County. After a strong blow, look from the ground for missing or creased shingles and debris in the yard, and have a roofer check the rest. Our wind damage page explains more.

What happens when I call the roofing line from Corinth?

Day or night, an automated assistant picks up and checks that the call is about a roof, then asks what you are seeing and where you live. Next it transfers you to an independent, locally owned roofing company that works in Corinth. That company inspects, prices the job and does the work, and you pay it. DFW Expert Roofers charges callers nothing and may be paid a referral fee.

Roof trouble in Corinth? Call the free line

Say what the roof is doing and which town you are in. The automated assistant passes you to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works in DFW. That company comes out, looks at the roof and prices the job itself.
